tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Every category ChainChoice ranks, with how many products it ranks, how many it assessed and left out with a reason, its leader, and its page.

tools.name: get_ranking
tools.description: The published order of one category: rank, product id, name and ChainChoice Score, with the methodology version, the dimension weights and what was assessed. The same order the category page and rankings.json publish.

tools.name: get_ranking_for_country
tools.description: The category's products as a reader in one country sees them: those available there, in order, with each one's published score and rank beside it. When nothing passes the country's availability filter, resultMode is "fallback" and the rows are the published order, none confirmed for that country.

tools.name: get_evidence
tools.description: For one category (and optionally one product id): each criterion, its weight, and per product the score with the quoted passage, its source URL and the day it was read.

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Checks a signed receipt (as ChainChoice serves it, or an issuer envelope) against the keys ChainChoice publishes: whether its content hash matches and its signature is valid. The same verifier as POST /api/v1/verify.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Reads a query exactly as ChainChoice's search bars do (the same resolver as the homepage, the navigation field and the command palette) and returns that reading: the page it opens (a category's ranked list with the country, monthly volume, sort and filters read from the words, a product's verdict, a

tools.name: hand_off
tools.description: Once the reader has agreed to go to a provider (consent: true), returns what to hand over: the provider's own address as ChainChoice's catalog records it (never a referral or affiliate link; ChainChoice earns nothing from it), the product's published rank and ChainChoice Score, the reader's country

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_evidence · Private data: hand_off · Public sink: get_ranking, verify_receipt · Destructive: search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_evidence · Private data: hand_off · Public sink: get_ranking, verify_receipt · Destructive: search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
